name: Bakbuk
overview: Bakbuk was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role as a temple servant highlights his participation in the religious duties associated with the Levitical priesthood during the post-exilic period. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Bakbuk means "gurgling (sound coming out of a bottle)." This proper name is recorded in Ezra 2:51 and does not indicate that it was given by God. The meaning reflects a distinctive Hebrew name but no further theological significance is noted.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Bakbuk as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the Levitical lineage. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no other family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Bakbuk's significance lies in his role as a temple servant within the tribe of Levi during the return from exile, as documented in Ezra 2:51. His mention underscores the restoration of Levitical service and worship in the post-exilic community. Although a minor figure, Bakbuk represents the faithful continuation of God's appointed priestly duties.
